clue.text: Benefactor at large bash I watch gamble

indicators.note: to bash something is to knock it out of shape, so these letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A patron of the arts throws a party where a guest stakes money on a timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a noun for a party, but it is the signal to rearrange I WATCH GAMBLE. Abel Magwitch is the escaped convict in Dickens's Great Expectations who secretly funds Pip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's convict is Pip's secret patron and an escaped prisoner, so he is a benefactor who is on the run.

clue.text: Long ago, a good doctor from Milan with a suitable qualification was promoted

definitions.text: Long ago, a good doctor from Milan

parts.note: a Bachelor of Medicine degree, MB, is the right qualification for a doctor
to have risen in rank is to have been promoted

explanation.surface: Long ago a physician from Milan, properly qualified, won advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'doctor' here is a Doctor of the Church: Saint Ambrose was the fourth-century Bishop of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Ambrose, fourth-century bishop of Milan, is one of the original Doctors of the Church, a title for great theologians.

clue.text: Singer in ELO left abandoned muse

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, as the word in the clue says
the letter for left is dropped and abandoned from the band's initials

parts.note: an informer who sings to the police is a rat

explanation.surface: A vocalist from the Electric Light Orchestra deserts the group, leaving a goddess behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a vocalist in the band, but it is an informer who sings to the police. 'left abandoned' leaves EO, and 'in' sets the informer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one who presides over lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: "Now with bright holly all your temples strow, With laurel green and sacred -" (John Gay)

definitions.text: "Now with bright holly all your temples strow, With laurel green and sacred -" (John Gay)

parts.words: "Now with bright holly all your temples strow, With laurel green and sacred -" (John Gay)
parts.note: the blank in John Gay's lines on Christmas decoration is a sacred evergreen plant linked with druids, filled in to complete the couplet

explanation.surface: Lines from John Gay's poem Trivia about decking churches with seasonal greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word completes Gay's line and rhymes with 'strow'.
explanation.definitionFit: The parasitic plant hung at Christmas was sacred to the druids, which is why Gay calls it sacred beside holly and laurel.

clue.text: Writer who's above stealing drop of red for debauched hedonist

indicators.note: taking something in, as a thief does, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: John Gay, quoted in the clue placed directly above this one

indicators.note: just a small drop of the word, its opening letter

explanation.surface: An author living upstairs pinches a splash of red wine, the reprobate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer who's above' points to 3 Down, which quotes John Gay. Dorian Gray is Oscar Wilde's corrupt pleasure-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's Dorian stays young while his portrait records a life of vice, the model of a dissolute pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: Odd new skill which writers might use for their work

definitions.text: which writers might use for their work

indicators.note: something odd is out of the normal pattern, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A strange new talent that authors could put to use in their craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like a comment on the skill, but it signals that NEW SKILL is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Before fountain pens, writers dipped their nibs into small pots of ink set into desks.

clue.text: Vessel coming around in narrow estuary at the front

indicators.note: the letter at the front of each of these five words is taken

explanation.surface: A boat turns about inside a tight river mouth near the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' is the definition, not part of the picture: the Caine is the minesweeper in Herman Wouk's novel The Caine Mutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wouk's novel the USS Caine is the warship whose officers relieve Captain Queeg of command.

clue.text: Error that could be made by confused type in road race

definitions.text: Error that could be made by confused type

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI in crosswords
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: A mistake that a muddled runner might make during a street race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' means printing type, not a kind of person. The M1 is Britain's longest-established motorway, London to Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter's slip that puts wrong letters on the page is a typographical mistake.

clue.text: A guy like Dr Frank Bryant is a fit young man

parts.note: Frank Bryant, the tutor in Willy Russell's play Educating Rita, is a university lecturer, a don

explanation.surface: A man resembling the jaded professor of Educating Rita turns out to be an attractive youth.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a hairdresser taught by a drinking Open University tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name is used for any handsome young man.

clue.text: Prince charged by revolutionary informants in Bolshevik's case

indicators.note: the middle part goes inside the outer letters, as the clue says
the outer letters of the word form a case around the rest

parts.note: to charge is to rush forward, so charged is ran

indicators.note: turning over as in a revolution, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rats are informers who tell on others

explanation.surface: A royal is accused by Bolshevik spies during a communist's trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' fits the Bolshevik picture but turns RATS to STAR. Bran Stark is a prince of Winterfell in George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is a younger son of Lord Eddard Stark of Winterfell, a royal heir in Martin's fantasy saga.

clue.text: One young guy touring India could be epic

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: going round something, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a lad is a young man
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A youth on a trip around the subcontinent might have a heroic adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is the founding long heroic narrative of Western literature.

clue.text: Old books about powerless European Peter, or Lawrence?

indicators.note: turned about, so this short word is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

indicators.note: the letter P, for power, is removed from the word

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: Ancient volumes on a Pole who has lost his strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter, or Lawrence?' points to the actor Peter, who played T. E. Lawrence in Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish actor Peter made his name as the title character in David Lean's 1962 film Lawrence of Arabia.

clue.text: Timeless character the Queen brought aboard favourite vessel

indicators.note: taken on board a ship, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
a pan is a cooking vessel
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch is taken on board her beloved ship by an ageless hero.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's boy who never grows up lives outside time in Neverland.

clue.text: In Jerusalem, met tiresome husband of Rosalie Hale

indicators.note: the letters sit inside these words, running across them

explanation.surface: A traveller in the Holy City encounters someone dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosalie Hale and Emmett Cullen are vampires married to each other in Stephenie Meyer's Twilight novels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Meyer's Twilight series Rosalie is wed to the burly vampire Emmett Cullen.

clue.text: Soldiers to visit seaside town briefly in March

indicators.note: going in to visit, so one piece is placed inside the other
cut short by removing its final letter

parts.note: Margate is a resort town on the Kent coast
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops go to a coastal resort for a short spring trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in March' looks like a date but is the definition: Margaret (Meg) is the eldest of the March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women. Margate is a Kent seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Meg, the eldest sister in Little Women, is Margaret March by full name.

clue.text: Sickly leader with cold praises nurses in uniforms primarily

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: holds within as a nurse holds a baby, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to laud is to praise

indicators.note: the first letters of these two words are taken

explanation.surface: An ailing boss, chilly, applauds nursing staff in their uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' fits the hospital picture but is a verb meaning holds. Claudius was the Roman emperor famed for limping and ill health.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor, whose story Robert Graves told in I, Claudius, was a frail invalid who became ruler.

clue.text: Foreign articles with passion for story of a fighting unit

parts.note: UN is the French indefinite article, a
DER is the German definite article, the
fire is ardour or passion

explanation.surface: Overseas newspaper pieces written with feeling about a military squad.
explanation.walkthrough: Under Fire is Henri Barbusse's 1916 novel following a French infantry squad in the First World War trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbusse's war novel tells of a squad of French soldiers in the trenches.

clue.text: A curt lie upset the victim of Tarquin's desires

indicators.note: knocked over and thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brusque untruth disturbed the woman wronged by a Roman prince.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend and Shakespeare's poem, the noblewoman raped by Sextus Tarquinius led to the founding of the Republic.

clue.text: Mongrel rescuer protected black watchdog

indicators.note: kept safe inside, so one piece surrounds the other
a mongrel is a mixed breed, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A mixed-breed dog that saved someone guarded a dark hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mongrel' and 'watchdog' paint one dog, but 'Mongrel' signals that RESCUER is mixed up. Cerberus is the three-headed hound guarding the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth's many-headed hound guards the gates of Hades, letting the dead in and no one out.

clue.text: Dom Manuel's biographer is around, being on call

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: CA, circa, means around or about a date
a bell is a call, as in give someone a bell

explanation.surface: The man who wrote Dom Manuel's life is nearby, taking a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: James Branch Cabell wrote Figures of Earth, the life of Dom Manuel of Poictesme. 'Give me a bell' is British slang for phone me.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote the fantasy chronicle of Dom Manuel, the swineherd who became Count of Poictesme.

clue.text: News chief travelled back to cover appeal

indicators.note: one piece covers the other by going around it
travelling back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rode means travelled on a horse or vehicle
it means sex appeal, as in the 1920s it girl

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss made a return trip to deal with a plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' looks like a legal plea but is IT, the old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper decides what news it carries.

clue.text: I released Secret Water and an audiobook version of Atonement

indicators.note: an audiobook is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: ransom in its old sense is the price of redemption or atonement

explanation.surface: A publisher boasts of issuing a novel and a spoken recording of Ian McEwan's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Secret Water is a 1939 book by Arthur Ransome, author of Swallows and Amazons. Atonement is Ian McEwan's novel, but here it is a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome wrote Secret Water, one of his Swallows and Amazons sailing adventures for children.

clue.text: Writer reprobate put in grave without regrets essentially

indicators.note: outside, in its old sense, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a bad one is a reprobate

indicators.note: the central letter, the essence, of the word

parts.note: to bury is to put in a grave

explanation.surface: A scoundrel was laid to rest with no remorse at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray Bradbury, author of Fahrenheit 451, and the novelist Malcolm Bradbury both wrote fiction.

clue.text: Invest pound in big economic upturn for ad canvasser

indicators.note: to invest is to put money in, so one piece goes inside another
the word in shows where the money goes

parts.note: a boom is a period of rapid economic growth
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: Put money into a strong recovery, advises the advertising salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Leopold Bloom, hero of James Joyce's Ulysses, sells newspaper advertising space in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's Leopold makes his living selling newspaper advertisements around Dublin.

clue.text: Heroic tragedy exponent needing drink to get Potter half-cut!

parts.note: someone who is dry is thirsty and needs a drink

indicators.note: the word is cut in half, its last three letters going

parts.note: Dennis Potter was the playwright of The Singing Detective

explanation.surface: Someone thirsty wants a drink to get the potter tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the drinking picture, but here it halves DENNIS. Dennis Potter was a British TV dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden wrote heroic plays such as The Conquest of Granada, the genre of rhymed heroic tragedy.

clue.text: Medic mum needing blood-type infusion can create this

definitions.text: Medic mum needing blood-type infusion can create this

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
A is one of the blood groups
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A doctor whose mother needs a transfusion can make quite a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a doctor and an ailing mother needing blood make a stage story.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital crisis with a mother in need of blood is the stuff of a play or TV serial.

clue.text: Queen who's seen in Hue area on occasion

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A monarch spotted now and then in the region of Hue.
explanation.walkthrough: Hue is a city in Vietnam, making the surface a travel note.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Olympian gods as wife of Zeus.

clue.text: "And a man prefers to say it: 'tis a manly — tell, / For the folks may be persuaded that you're doing very well" (Henry Lawson)

definitions.text: "And a man prefers to say it: 'tis a manly — tell, / For the folks may be persuaded that you're doing very well" (Henry Lawson)

parts.words: "And a man prefers to say it: 'tis a manly — tell, / For the folks may be persuaded that you're doing very well" (Henry Lawson)
parts.note: the blank in Lawson's verse is a short phrase meaning deceive, the kind of telling that makes people think you are prospering

explanation.surface: Lines by the Australian poet Henry Lawson about putting on a brave face.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing two words make 'a manly lie to tell'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive someone with a false account is to tell them an untruth.

clue.text: Somehow I'm ok with death in comic opera

indicators.note: arranged in some way or other, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Somehow I feel fine, even with the end approaching, in a light operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera, where death by beheading is played for laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's 1885 light opera set in Japan is the best known of their comic works.

clue.text: Bit of mismanagement and a lame header disturbed Chester fan

indicators.note: things that are disturbed are thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
only a small bit of the word, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A slice of poor management and a weak headed goal upset a football supporter of Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chester fan' suggests a supporter of Chester City football club, but Emma Haredale in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge loves Edward Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: In Barnaby Rudge Emma is in love with Edward Chester despite their families' feud, so she is his devoted admirer.
